A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CHG research, with readable text, equations, figures and tables. V1 ends with references; v2 additionally includes technical appendices and a checklist. The supplied material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original head-ablation experiments, head-role distributions, comparisons with causal mediation analysis, and contrastive gating results across language-model tasks.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results in Section 4, Figures 2–5 and Table 2. Results retained from v1 still constitute original empirical evidence.

M1.justification: The core CHG procedure is unchanged, but Section 4.4 revises the stated CCHG objective from a difference of two regularized losses to a retain/forget log-probability contrast with one explicit regularizer. This changes the written objective without establishing that the implementation or experiments changed.

E1.justification: Both versions use OpenMathInstruct2, BIG-Bench syntax, CommonsenseQA, six function-vector tasks, and ABA/ABB symbolic reasoning. Appendix 6.1 documents existing subsets and prompt construction; it does not establish additional task or dataset coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparisons remain CMA for function-vector and symbolic-reasoning tasks, and ungated versus CCHG-gated models. Newly discussed differentiable masking, LoFiT and Gumbel-based pruning are not added as experimental comparators.

E3.justification: Section 4.4 changes the stated CCHG regularization setting from λ < 0 to λ > 0, although v2 Appendix 6.2 specifies λ = -0.1. This is an internally inconsistent revision to the reported training specification, not evidence of rerunning experiments. Evaluation models, metrics and held-out-task design remain unchanged; other appendix settings are newly disclosed.

E4.justification: The targeted head ablations, role-distribution and consistency analyses, CMA agreement analysis, and cross-task CCHG experiments are retained. The new appendix supplies procedural details without adding ablations, robustness tests or supplementary empirical analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report 10 seeds per model-dataset pair, 10 CHG masks per function-vector task, 20 per ABA/ABB task, CMA significance tests and 95% confidence intervals in Figure 5. New discussion of bootstrapping does not introduce a reported bootstrap analysis or uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Figures 2–5 and Table 2 retain the same results. Numerical findings also match, including CMA t-statistics of 8.52 and 11.18 and the singular-plural retained-format accuracies of 92% and 21% under the respective CCHG conditions. No new evaluation-result entries are added.

T1.justification: Equation 2 changes mathematically: the identical regularizers cancel in v1's difference of CHG losses, whereas v2 explicitly retains one regularization term. This revises the formal loss definition. Equation 1 and the head-role formulas remain unchanged; neither version adds theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The introduction changes 'low-overlap' circuits to circuits with 'varying degrees of overlap' and qualifies selective suppression as context-dependent and occurring without 'substantially' disrupting the other mode. It also adds a distribution-estimation motivation for repeated fits. The central CHG and CCHG contributions remain.

C2.justification: V2 expands the existing interaction-based interpretation, presenting gate divergence and across-run variability as informative features and motivating a bootstrapped view of contingent circuits. The Discussion develops CHG's role as a first-pass diagnostic while retaining its inability to explain individual heads' precise computations.

D1.justification: V2 adds repository access information and Appendices 6.1–6.3 covering filtering, splits, prompts, initialization, Adam learning-rate schedules, batch sizes, update counts, clipping, hardware and runtime estimates. These substantially expand reproducibility documentation absent from v1. The CCHG regularization sign nevertheless conflicts between the main text and appendix.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands positioning against closely related differentiable masking, LoFiT and Gumbel-based pruning, asserting that CHG preserves joint head dependencies that factorized gating misses. Six references are added overall, including these methodological sources, Talking Heads and Adam; existing references are retained.

P1.justification: V2 makes targeted language corrections, rewrites portions of the Discussion, expands related-work explanations, and adds acknowledgments, technical appendices and a checklist. The main section sequence and experimental narrative remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: All five figures and both tables are retained with unchanged graphical content and table structure. Several displays move through page reflow, and Figure 1's caption newly identifies L3.2-3BI and OpenMathInstruct2. The conference footer and additional back matter also change the layout.

improvement.justification: The new technical appendix and code-access information improve reproducibility, while qualified contribution statements better reflect the existing task-dependent findings. However, the revised CCHG specification remains ambiguous: Section 4.4 states λ > 0, whereas Appendix 6.2 uses λ = -0.1. The documentation gains support a net improvement, but this unresolved objective inconsistency limits it.
